A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OFER and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The retained content can be matched despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on NoW, CO-545, and the Dey dataset, together with ranking and architecture ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds diversity, plausibility, real-occlusion, and image-embedding evaluations.

M1.justification: The IdGen–IdRank–ExpGen procedure is retained. However, v2 appendix Figure 12 specifies 53 ExpGen parameters, including three jaw coefficients, whereas v1 and v2's main text specify 50. The PDFs do not resolve whether this represents a model change or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: v2 adds the real-world occluded-face dataset of Erakin et al., covering masks, sunglasses, and natural occlusions (Section 4.1, Table 5). This extends coverage within the existing reconstruction task; the training datasets, NoW, CO-545, and Dey dataset remain.

E2.justification: MoFA disappears from the NoW comparison, and MICA's neutral CO-545 results disappear from Table 3. CLIP and DINOv2 are added as encoder comparators in v2 Table 7. Several other neutral reconstruction baselines are merely moved from the appendix into the consolidated main table.

E3.justification: Expression evaluation expands beyond reconstruction RMSE to closest-sample error, visible and occluded self-distance, shape diversity, and distribution-based plausibility metrics (v2 Section 4.3). The new evaluation without ground-truth meshes uses 200 images per occlusion category. Existing training budgets and NoW splits are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ArcFace-versus-CLIP/DINOv2 ablation (Table 7) and a case study comparing masked and minimally occluded images of one identity (Figure 7). Existing ranking-mixture, sample-count, input-representation, and loss ablations are retained, with some moved into the main text.

E5.justification: Both versions report descriptive reconstruction-error standard deviations without repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new STD-S measure evaluates diversity among generated shapes rather than uncertainty in experimental estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical results for diversity and plausibility (Tables 4–5), encoder comparisons (Table 7), and NoW subset minima and averages. Table 3 changes OFER's occluded expressive CO-545 RMSE from 2.97 to 2.78; this is a reported-value revision, not an established same-protocol improvement. Most existing ranking and NoW test results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 introduces mathematical definitions for the added evaluation measures, including the ASD-O harmonic mean in Equation 7. The ranking formulation also changes its written error definition from mean vertex displacement to an L1 norm and replaces v1's index-inconsistent ground-truth softmax expression. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain two conditional diffusion models, ranking to select a consistent identity, and CO-545. Claims of plausible, diverse reconstructions and superiority over occlusion-based methods retain their scope; the new evaluations principally add supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 adds limitations concerning softmax score dilution with large candidate sets, explains why expressions are not ranked, and attributes CLIP/DINOv2's weaker results to their broader training domains. It also replaces the specific difficulty with negative expressions with a broader qualification about missing expressive detail.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents 1000-step DDPM sampling, a five-layer ranking MLP, detailed U-Net residual/convolution blocks, and 15 expression samples per evaluated image, and adds a project website pointer. Conversely, v1's explicit 1785-vertex count and sinusoidal-conditioning description are no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the real-occlusion dataset, CLIP/DINOv2 comparisons, diffusion background, and diversity metrics, while removing references such as SCConv. The principal positioning against Diverse3D and the claimed novelty of ranking diffusion samples remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The method description, especially IdRank, is extensively rewritten. Preliminaries move inside Method, IdGen and IdRank evaluations are combined, ranking-ablation discussion moves into the main text, and new appendix sections organize design choices and architecture details.

P2.justification: v2 redraws overview and ranking diagrams, merges the generative-network diagrams, and adds a detailed architecture figure and single-identity comparison. It consolidates v1 Tables 1, 2, and 10 into Table 2 and substantially rearranges qualitative results and ablation displays between the main text and appendix.

improvement.justification: The added diversity/plausibility evaluations and encoder ablation provide more direct support for the existing claims, while the rewritten exposition improves readability. These benefits yield a limited net improvement: v2 introduces conflicting 50-versus-53-dimensional ExpGen descriptions, and its ASD-O variable definitions conflict with their stated visible/occluded roles, limiting the clarity and reproducibility of some additions.
